text:
sara: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — proposal sketch: introduce a lightweight 'reheat' token that temporarily prevents eviction for prefixes after a cold miss, to reduce churn during short bursts. thoughts?

james: curious, how is this different from the soft-pin we already discussed?

sara: good q. soft-pin today is tenant-scoped and long-lived. reheat is prefix-scoped, very short (250-2000ms), auto-expiring, and only granted on successful prefill/rehydration to avoid keeping dead prefixes.

kiran: sounds promising. main risk I see is holding slabs and increasing memory pressure during coordinated bursts. do we have a backpressure signal?

sara: plan is admission-limited: reheat grants are probabilistic under high occupancy, plus we expose a per-slab watermark to the allocator so reheat can be refused when slab free < X%.

ella: implementation nit: we should avoid a global coordinator. can reheat be an opaque token attached to prefix metadata and validated locally?

sara: yes — token is just a monotonic lease id + expiry. no leader required. local eviction checks consult token expiry and slab watermark.

maria: how does this play with cross-node handoff? if node A rehydrates and gets a reheat token but hands off to node B, do we carry the token?

sara: two options: 1) tokens are transferable with prefix ownership metadata, or 2) tokens are non-transferable and lost on handoff (so handoff must detect recent reheat and decide to rehydrate on target). leaning toward transferable to avoid re-stealing hot prefix immediately.

james: transferable token increases correctness surface — need to ensure we don't double-count residency or bypass quota. maybe attach a 'reheat-origin' and require target to honor but decrement local admission budget?

kiran: can we encode a small amortized cost in the token so the allocator accounts for memory? e.g., token includes reserved_bytes or a credit counter.

sara: yup, token payload could be: `lease_id|expiry|reserved_bytes|origin_node`. kept tiny.

ella: what about eviction fairness? with reheat, small tenants with spikey traffic could hog reheat grants and cause hotspotting. add per-tenant short-term cap?

sara: we already have per-tenant eviction credits; reheat would consume from that budget. if exhausted, reheat denied. prevents freeloading.

maria: operational question: how do we observe reheat activity? need metrics: granted_count, denied_count_by_reason, avg_reserved_bytes, reheat-to-evict ratio. also tracing on token transfer.

sara: agreed. will add metrics and a new trace span `kv.reheat.grant` with attrs (tenant, prefix_hash, reserved_bytes, origin_node). ops-bot anything to add?

ops-bot: reminder: new metric names must follow prefix `redwood.kv.` and be added to the ingestion whitelist before rollout.

james: one more tradeoff: expiry jitter. if all reheats expire at same ms we could get synchronized evictions. add randomized backoff on expiry + elastic grace that extends with active hits.

sara: propose expiry = base + rand(0, base/4) and extend-on-hit up to max_extension. extension consumes additional reservation credits.

kiran: sounds safe. last concern: correctness around read-after-write ordering when token is transferred during in-flight writes. any invariants we need?

sara: maintain write lease ordering: handoff must publish a handoff fence that denotes last applied seq before transfer. reheat token should carry `fence_seq` so target knows whether recent writes are visible. if mismatch, target performs a conservative rehydrate path before honoring reheat.

ella: OK. for the RFC follow-up doc: I'll draft a narrow spec that covers token format, admission rules, transfer protocol, and metric list. will include a small state machine diagram.

sara: perfect. please include two microbenchmarks: (1) bursty tiny-prefix workload showing evict reduction and (2) failure-case where transfer lost token -> correctness probe.

maria: ops will add telemetry dashboards and a canary for slab-watermark alarms.

james: +1 to incremental rollout: feature flag gated, default-off for Dedicated customers, opt-in via runtime config.

ella: I'll draft today and ping reviewers. thanks all :rocket:
